cmd.audit.long:
Launches an opencode session with the auditor agent to perform an audit.

Available audit types:
  security       Vulnerabilities, injections, secret management, dependencies
  performance    Memory leaks, N+1, rendering, bundle size, lazy loading
  architecture   Coupling, cohesion, patterns, layers, technical debt
  accessibility  WCAG, ARIA, contrast, keyboard navigation, screen readers
  ecodesign      Carbon footprint, resource weight, unnecessary requests, green patterns
  observability  Logs, traces, metrics, alerting, correlation, SLI/SLO
  privacy        GDPR, personal data, consent, retention, minimization

  # To load for every session:

Fish:
  $ oh completion fish | source

  $ oh completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/oh.fish

cmd.init.preamble:
Welcome to oh — OpenHub CLI

To configure the hub, you will need:

LLM Provider (one required)
  • Amazon Bedrock : configured AWS profile (~/.aws/credentials) or bearer token
  • Anthropic      : API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
  • OpenRouter     : API key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY)
  • GitHub Copilot : active Copilot access (gh auth)

MCP Servers (optional)
  • Figma          : personal access token (scope file:read)
  • GitLab         : personal access token (scope api)
  • Google Slides  : OAuth access token

Everything can be configured later:
  oh provider setup — provider credentials
  oh mcp setup      — MCP tokens

cmd.team.init.long:
Launch an interactive wizard to configure team collaboration.

The wizard configures 4 adaptive steps:
  1. Global config (takeover, sessions)
  2. Identity (team registration)
  3. Mattermost notifications (optional)
  4. Team policies (automated conventions)

The team-state repo must be created beforehand on GitLab/GitHub.
If the repo is already configured, only relevant steps are offered.

cmd.remote.setup.short: Creates or validates the oh-runner project of a GitLab group (pipeline, trigger, variables)
cmd.remote.setup.long: Checks GitLab API access, creates or validates the oh-runner project of the group, writes the pipeline generated by oh, creates the trigger token (kept in the keychain) and sets the masked CI variables: LLM key of the jobs (--llm), access token of each target project (--project, write_repository and read_api scopes), team-state token (--teamstate). Secrets are read from the terminal (hidden input) or from an environment variable (--*-env), never from arguments. Can be run again: only what is missing or changed is modified.

cmd.remote.setup.flags.url: GitLab instance URL (default: the one of the current repository)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.group: full path of the served group (default: the one of the current repository)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.builder: project image builder: kaniko (default) or dind
cmd.remote.setup.flags.token_key: keychain key of an existing GitLab token (api scope)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.token_env: environment variable holding the GitLab token (api scope)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.no_create: do not create the oh-runner project when it is missing
cmd.remote.setup.flags.force: replace a .gitlab-ci.yml that was not generated by oh
cmd.remote.setup.flags.llm: set the LLM key of the jobs (hidden input)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.llm_provider: LLM provider of the jobs: bedrock (default), anthropic, openrouter
cmd.remote.setup.flags.llm_key_env: environment variable holding the LLM key of the jobs
cmd.remote.setup.flags.project: target project whose access token to set (full path, repeatable)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.project_token_env: environment variable holding the project token (single --project)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.teamstate: set the write token of the team-state repository (hidden input)
cmd.remote.setup.flags.teamstate_token_e: environment variable holding the team-state token
cmd.remote.setup.flags.oh_binary: Linux oh binary to upload for development builds

cmd.session.fetch.short: Fetches a finished remote session (artifacts, import to resume it locally)
cmd.session.fetch.long: Downloads the artifacts of the oh-runner pipeline (Beads journal, summary, session export) and imports the session into a local server (worktree of the branch pushed by the job) to resume it with oh session attach. The Beads journal is not replayed here: oh session resolve, with confirmation.

cmd.session.resolve.short: Replays the Beads journal of a fetched remote session (conflicts, confirmation)
cmd.session.resolve.long: Each Beads write of the session is checked again (workflow beads.allow, refused options, tickets of the session) then applied on the machine after confirmation. A ticket changed on the machine since sending is a conflict: keep the local version, apply the remote one, or merge the notes only. Can be run again: only the remaining writes are applied.

cmd.session.resolve.flags.apply_remote: conflicting tickets whose remote writes are applied
cmd.session.resolve.flags.merge_notes: conflicting tickets whose notes only are merged
cmd.session.resolve.flags.all: resolution of every conflict: keep-local | apply-remote | merge-notes
cmd.session.resolve.flags.dry_run: show the replay without applying anything
cmd.session.resolve.confirm: Apply %d Beads write(s) on the machine?
cmd.session.resolve.failed: %d write(s) failed: fix then run oh session resolve %s again
